text.p: Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy Monday reported first quarter earnings down 46 percent on the year-ago period, but said it saw improving profitability in the second half.

Metsa-Serla -- Finland's third largest forestry group -- said first quarter profit after one-time items fell to 129 million markka ($25.5 million) from 239 million ($47.23 million) in the year-ago period.

"The fall in profit is due to the fact that prices for almost all products, but particularly for market pulp and coated magazine paper, were considerably lower than last year," Metsa-Serla said in a statement.
"Our expectations for the future are optimistic," group President Jorma Vaajoki said in an interview.
Metsa-Serla said it expected "favorable profitability development during the second half of 1997, providing the positive market development continues."
Group net sales rose to 3.93 billion markka ($777 million) in January-March from 3.75 billion ($741 million) a year ago.
